$comment: The text around a selection, as every implementation of the Librarian must cut it: a text, what an annotation's target selects of it, a window, and the text before the selection, the selection, and the text after it. Every Librarian runs every case and fails on a difference, in whatever language it is written. A case has one of two parts, `around` or `gathered`, for the two places the Librarian cuts a text around an annotation. THE CUT, which both make. A selection is from a `start` to an `end`, offsets into the text that count Unicode code points from its start, as specs/src/text/offset-cases.json states an offset. A window says how much text to take on each side, and counts code points too. `before` is the text from `start` less the window, or from the start of the text where that is nearer, up to `start`. `selected` is the text from `start` to `end`. `after` is the text from `end` to `end` and the window, or to the end of the text where that is nearer. A text with a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is what tells this count from a count of UTF-16 code units or of bytes, so the cases have such characters before, inside and after a selection. WHAT A CASE STATES. `text` is the text. `selector` is what the annotation's target states: one selector, or several, or none where the target states no selector. `context` is the answer: `before`, `selected` and `after`. WHERE THE SELECTION IS, which both cuts decide by one rule. The first position selector the target states is the place, wherever among its selectors it is: its `start` and its `end`. A target with no position selector is placed by the first quote selector it states, whose `exact` words are found in the text as specs/src/annotations/reconcile-cases.json states a quote is found: where the text has them once, there; where it has them more than once, at the first place its `prefix` and its `suffix` fit, and at the first place of all where it states neither or neither fits; and where the text does not have them as written, where a looser search finds them, and the selection is then the text's own words. Words the text has nowhere place nothing, and neither does a target that states no selector or only a selector of another kind. AROUND is the cut the Librarian makes where it summarizes an annotation. `window` states how much to take `before` and `after`, each its own count. `refused` in place of a context says there is no answer and the cut fails: a summary is of a passage, and a target that nothing places has none. GATHERED is the cut in a gathered context, which states it as its focus's `selected`: `before`, the selection as `text`, and `after`. `window` is one count, taken on both sides. A window less than 100 or more than 5000 is `refused`, and nothing is cut. A target that nothing places gives no selection, and the context is null: the gathered context states no `selected`, and is still an answer. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: a selection in the middle of a text, with a window on each side shorter than the text there: each side is as long as its own window
a selection at the start of a text has nothing before it
a selection at the end of a text has nothing after it
a window larger than the text takes all there is on each side, and no more
a window of nothing takes the selection alone
a selection of the whole text has nothing on either side
an empty selection selects nothing, and has the text on each side of the place it is at
an empty selection at the end of a text: an offset may be the length of the text
a text with nothing in it has one place, and nothing around it
characters outside the basic plane before the selection: each is one code point, so the selection is its own words and the window before it is 2 code points, a book and a space
characters outside the basic plane inside the selection: a selection of 2 code points is the two books whole
characters outside the basic plane after the selection: a window of 3 code points after it is a space and the two books whole
the length of a text is its count of code points: a selection that ends at 7 ends this text, which is 9 UTF-16 code units
a window larger than a text with characters outside the basic plane takes all of it, each character whole
a target that states a position selector and a quote selector of the same span is cut at the position
a target with a quote selector and no position selector is cut where the text has its words
words the text has twice are found where the quote's suffix fits: the second place, which has the suffix beside it, and not the first, which has it more than 32 code points on

around.text: The fox ran over the hill and far away into the dark wood. A second fox slept.

cases.why: a quote selector whose words the text has nowhere is refused here: nothing places the annotation
a target that states no selector is refused here
in a gathered context, a position selector is cut at its offsets, and a window of 100 on a shorter text takes all of it
a target that states a position selector and a quote selector of the same span gathers the one cut
a quote selector's words are found in the text, and the cut is around them
words found at the start of the text have nothing before them
words found at the end of the text have nothing after them
words the text does not have give no selection: the gathered context states none, and is not a failure
words found after characters outside the basic plane are selected whole: where they are is counted in code points
words that are characters outside the basic plane are found and selected whole
words found before characters outside the basic plane have them after, each whole
the window around found words is 100 code points on each side: ten of the twelve runs of a book and nine digits, which are 110 UTF-16 code units
the window around a position is 100 code points on each side too: the position is 120 code points into this text, and 132 UTF-16 code units
a window of 5000 is the largest a gathered context takes
a window of 99 is less than a gathered context takes: it is refused
a window of 5001 is more than a gathered context takes: it is refused
words the text has twice are found where the quote's prefix fits: the second place, and not the first

gathered.text: The fox ran. A second fox slept.

cases.why: words the text has twice, in a quote that states no prefix and no suffix, are found at the first place

gathered.text: The fox ran. A second fox slept.

cases.why: words the text has in another letter case are found, and the selection is the text's own words
a position selector is the place wherever among the selectors it is: stated after a selector of another kind, it is still read
a position selector stated after a quote selector of other words is the place: the position is read before any quote
a target that states no selector selects nothing of the text: the gathered context states no selection
a selector that is neither a position nor a quote selects nothing of a text: the gathered context states no selection
